content: Android Central, a blog focused on the Android ecosystem, laid off its staff yesterday, but owner Future confirms to The Verge that the site will continue publishing. Yesterday, four of the six staffers on Android Central’s staff page posted publicly about the layoffs, including Shruti Shekar, Derrek Lee, Harish Jonnalagadda, and Nicholas Sutrich, and former senior editor Namerah Saud Fatmi updated her LinkedIn to indicate that her tenure at Android Central had ended. Both Lee, the site’s managing editor, and Sutrich confirmed that all remaining staff were laid off. The former staffers weren’t told whether the site would shut down. Today, new posts have been published to the site, though they are from the site’s freelance contributors rather than the previous full-time staffers. “Future will continue to publish Android Central. We’ll share further information about the future of the site in due course,” Future spokesperson Nicole Martineau tells The Verge, adding: “We will not be providing any further comment at this time.” Android Police, another Android-focused blog, also laid off at least two staffers recently. The site currently lists an editorial team of four people. Valnet, which owns Android Police and previously purchased The Verge’s sister site Polygon, didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

chineseContent: Android Central 是一家专注于 Android 生态系统的博客，昨天解雇了员工，但所有者 Future 向 The Verge 证实该网站将继续发布内容。昨天，Android Central 员工页面上的六名员工中的四名公开发布了裁员消息，其中包括 Shruti Shekar、Derrek Lee、Harish Jonnalagadda 和 Nicholas Sutrich，前高级编辑 Namerah Saud Fatmi 更新了她的 LinkedIn，表示她在 Android Central 的任期已经结束。该网站的总编辑 Lee 和 Sutrich 均证实，所有剩余员工均已被解雇。前工作人员没有被告知该网站是否会关闭。今天，新的帖子已经发布到该网站，尽管它们来自该网站的自由撰稿人，而不是以前的全职员工。 “Future 将继续发布 Android Central。我们将在适当的时候分享有关该网站未来的更多信息，”Future 发言人 Nicole Martineau 告诉 The Verge，并补充道：“我们目前不会提供任何进一步的评论。”另一个专注于 Android 的博客 Android Police 最近也解雇了至少两名员工。该网站目前列出了一个由四人组成的编辑团队。 Valnet 拥有 Android Police，此前还收购了 The Verge 的姊妹网站 Polygon，该公司没有立即回复置评请求。
